They slam the lid shut, their jaw tight, and begin scraping the usable portions into a separate container, a muscle twitching in their cheek.

In the warehouse loading bay, a person must close an unfinished shift. A crucial shipment has arrived but the designated forklift is missing its charging cable, and the backup is also nowhere to be found. The person stares at the stacks of boxes, then slowly walks over to the office, their shoulders slumping slightly as they prepare to inform their supervisor about the delay.

In the library meeting table, a person must close an unfinished shift. A volunteer has just finished sorting a large collection of old photographs, but has inexplicably placed them all into mismatched numbered trays. The person looks at the jumbled stacks, then back at the volunteer who beams expectantly. A soft chuckle escapes them as they pick up the first tray, the corners of their mouth lifting.

In the storm shelter desk, a person must close an unfinished shift. A child, separated from their guardian during a drill, is now calmer but visibly distressed, clutching a worn teddy bear. The person offers the child a juice box from the supplies, their voice gentle and their gaze steady. They then make a note on the whiteboard to ensure reunification protocols are reviewed with staff immediately.
